inline_comments.comment: `slice(-limit)` removes from the beginning of `initialPresets` (the user-defined preset colors), not from the dynamically-selected colors at the end. With `maxPresetColors: 5` and 8 presets defined, the user sees presets 4–8 (Gold, Green, Seafoam, Purple, Ultraviolet) and never sees Coral, Ocean, or Orange. As the user picks colors during a session, their user-defined presets will be progressively displaced. With the default limit of 27 this was rarely an issue, but at small custom limits (e.g., 5–10) it is a significant UX problem. Consider reversing the strategy: cap `selectedColors` to `max(0, limit - initialPresets.length)` slots and always show all (or the first) `initialPresets` up to the limit.

Non-integer positive values (e.g., `maxPresetColors: 3.5`) silently fall back to 27 because `Number.isInteger(3.5)` is `false`. This is surprising — a user who passes `3.5` almost certainly intends "3 or 4" colors, not 27. Consider using `Math.floor(maxPresetColors)` to coerce floats gracefully: `const limit = Math.floor(maxPresetColors); return (limit > 0) ? combined.slice(-limit) : combined;`.

The internal `usePresets` hook's parameter type for `maxPresetColors` is inferred as `number` (with a `= 27` default). Adding an explicit type annotation `maxPresetColors: number = 27` would be more self-documenting and consistent with the other parameters in the signature, which are all explicitly typed.

The type `number` accepts `NaN`, `-Infinity`, and non-integer values, all of which silently fall back to 27. The JSDoc describes `0` and `Infinity` as special sentinels but doesn't mention that other edge cases (negatives, floats, `NaN`) silently fall back to the default. Consider extending the JSDoc: "Non-positive integers and non-integer values other than `Infinity` are treated as invalid and fall back to `27`."

`WithInvalidMaxPresetColors` only supplies 5 `presetColors`. Since the fallback is 27 and there are only 5 presets, there is no visible difference between this story and normal behavior — the user sees all 5 colors regardless of whether the limit is `-5` (→ 27) or any valid number ≥ 5. The story claims to demonstrate "falls back to 27," but it doesn't actually show the 27-limit capping anything. To make the fallback observable, use more than 27 presets so the cap visibly takes effect.

general_comments.comment: No unit tests are added for the modified `usePresets` hook behavior. The new parameter introduces several boundary conditions — `0`, `Infinity`, negative values, non-integer values, and values larger or smaller than the preset array length — all of which deserve test coverage to prevent regressions. The existing behavior of `slice(-27)` should also be verified as unchanged when `maxPresetColors` is omitted or `undefined`.

The `svelte-vite/package.json` peer dependency bump (`@sveltejs/vite-plugin-svelte ^7.0.0`) and the corresponding `yarn.lock` update are unrelated to the `ColorControl` feature. Bundling unrelated changes makes it harder to review, bisect, or revert. These should be in a separate PR.

The PR description states "Added two new stories demonstrating the feature (`WithMaxPresetColors` and `WithUnlimitedPresetColors`)" but the diff actually adds three stories — `WithMaxPresetColors`, `WithUnlimitedPresetColors`, and `WithInvalidMaxPresetColors`. The description should be updated to reflect all added stories.
